newsitem.title: FRANCE: Israel's Netanyahu hopes for Swiss holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu hopes for Swiss holocaust fund.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in an interview published on Tuesday he hoped Holocaust victims would be compensated for assets seized by the Nazis which later found their way into Swiss hands.

"We must, along with our Swiss counterparts, put mechanisms in place which will enable us to correct this terrible historical injustice," Netanyahu said ahead of a planned visit to Switzerland later this month.

"Six million Jews including a million children were exterminated and their goods pillaged. Any country in the world would try to obtain the restitution of their belongings," he said in the interview, published in the French daily Liberation.

Swiss Ambassador to Washington Carlo Jagmetti resigned on Monday after a Swiss newspaper revealed a confidential memo he had written stating that Switzerland was in a public relations "war" with Jews over the issue of goods and money seized by the Nazis and now believed to be in Swiss hands.
Switzerland has appointed a nine-member international panel of historians to review whether Switzerland acted honourably during World War Two or cynically profited from it, as critics have alleged.

Jagmetti's memo said the controversy over Switzerland's role was a public relations "war that Switzerland must wage and win" but it also argued that a payment should be made to the survivors of Holocaust victims.
Following Jagmetti's resignation, Swiss officials reassured Jewish leaders that such a fund would be established.
"We are not engaged in a commercial transaction," Netanyahu said. "This is a moral and ethical transaction. The question is to determine how we are going to resolve it.
"I have no answer at the present time but I hope to find a constructive attitude on the part of my Swiss counterparts, so that we can come up with a solution," Netanyahu said.
